title: Captain America: The First Avenger
instruction: STOP before credits — the credits scene belongs RIGHT BEFORE The Avengers
context: The origin of Steve Rogers and the first Infinity Stone (Tesseract). Sets the moral compass the Avengers are built around.

title: Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter
context: Fun post-WWII Peggy short. No story payoff beyond the main film.

title: Agent Carter (Season 1)
context: Peggy builds the SSR into what becomes S.H.I.E.L.D. Entertaining spy thriller — no thread leads to Doomsday.

title: Agent Carter (Season 2)
context: Zero Matter teases the Dark Dimension. Self-contained — no Doomsday thread.

title: X-Men: First Class
context: Xavier and Magneto's origin — their friendship, split, and divergent ideologies. Both confirmed for Doomsday with the original actors.

title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
instruction: Optional — Logan is the essential Wolverine film.
context: Wolverine's Weapon X origin — how Logan got his adamantium skeleton. Optional side-viewing in the Fox saga.

title: X-Men
context: The original X-Men film — Xavier's school, Magneto's Brotherhood, and the first clash. Introduces the full Fox cast confirmed returning for Doomsday.

title: X2: X-Men United
context: The best of the original trilogy. Stryker's war on mutants unites X-Men and Brotherhood. Jean Grey's sacrifice at the end sets up The Last Stand.

title: X-Men: The Last Stand
context: Jean Grey returns as the Phoenix. Xavier is killed. Magneto loses his powers. The entire Fox cast confirmed returning for Doomsday — Days of Future Past retcons this timeline.

title: The Wolverine
instruction: Optional — bridges The Last Stand to Days of Future Past.
context: Logan in Japan mourning Jean Grey. Its post-credits scene sets up Days of Future Past.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
context: Wolverine rewrites the X-Men timeline — erasing the dark future and restoring all the characters who died. Critical for understanding which version of the X-Men exists going into Doomsday.

title: X-Men: Apocalypse
instruction: Optional — continues the First Class and Days of Future Past timeline.
context: The young X-Men face En Sabah Nur — the first mutant — in 1983. Part of the rebooted timeline after Days of Future Past.

title: Dark Phoenix
instruction: Optional — the final film of the Fox X-Men saga.
context: Jean Grey's Phoenix arc in 1992 — the last Fox X-Men film before Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Captain Marvel
instruction: STOP before end-credits — post-credit scene belongs after Infinity War
context: Carol Danvers becomes the most powerful hero in the MCU. Her 1990s origin explains why she's been off-world — and why she answers when called.

title: Blade
context: Wesley Snipes' vampire hunter — the film that proved Marvel movies could work before the MCU existed. Snipes rumoured (unconfirmed) for a Doomsday or Secret Wars cameo.

title: Blade II
context: The superior sequel, directed by Guillermo del Toro. Expands the vampire world with the Reaper threat.

title: Blade: Trinity
context: Concludes Snipes' trilogy. Ryan Reynolds appears as Hannibal King — a completely different character from Deadpool.

title: Blade: The Series (Season 1)
context: Sticky Fingaz takes over as Blade for Spike TV, picking up loosely after the film trilogy. Detroit, the vampire House of Chthon, and Krista Starr investigating her brother's murder. Cancelled after one season and its own continuity — no thread reaches the MCU.

title: Spider-Man
instruction: Tobey Maguire's Spider-Man returns in No Way Home.
context: Tobey Maguire's Peter Parker origin, and the version of the character No Way Home brings back.

title: Spider-Man 2
context: The best of the Raimi trilogy. Peter's identity crisis and Doc Ock's redemption define who Tobey's Peter is when he returns.

title: Spider-Man 3
context: Concludes Tobey's arc. Harry Osborn dies a hero. The Venom symbiote makes its first screen appearance.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
instruction: Andrew Garfield's Spider-Man returns in No Way Home.
context: Andrew Garfield's Peter Parker origin. His guilt over Captain Stacy's death shapes the character who arrives in No Way Home.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
context: Gwen Stacy's death is the defining tragedy of Garfield's Peter — the wound No Way Home begins to heal.

title: Ghost Rider
context: Nicolas Cage as stunt rider Johnny Blaze — who sells his soul and becomes the Spirit of Vengeance. A standalone Sony/Columbia Marvel film with no connection to the MCU.

title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
context: The 2011 sequel — Johnny Blaze hunts the Devil across Eastern Europe. Standalone Sony/Columbia and disconnected from the MCU (the MCU Ghost Rider, Robbie Reyes, appears in Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.).

title: Daredevil (2003)
context: Ben Affleck's Matt Murdock, made by Fox years before Marvel Studios reclaimed the character. A separate continuity from the Charlie Cox Daredevil — no connection to the MCU version.

title: Elektra
context: Spin-off of the 2003 Daredevil, with Jennifer Garner reprising Elektra Natchios. Same separate Fox continuity.

title: The Punisher (2004)
context: Thomas Jane as Frank Castle, produced by Lionsgate. Unconnected to Jon Bernthal's MCU Punisher.

title: Punisher: War Zone
context: A hard reboot with Ray Stevenson as Frank Castle — a third separate Punisher continuity.

title: Man-Thing
context: Low-budget horror adaptation released direct to television in the US. Wholly standalone.

title: Fantastic Four (2005)
context: The 2005 Fox film — Reed Richards' team gains powers from cosmic radiation. Chris Evans plays Johnny Storm before he became Captain America. Standalone, no MCU connection.

title: Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer
context: The 2007 sequel — the team faces the Silver Surfer and Galactus. Chris Evans returns as the Human Torch. Standalone Fox Marvel, no MCU connection.

title: Hulk (2003)
context: Ang Lee's Universal-produced Hulk, five years before Marvel Studios rebooted the character in The Incredible Hulk. Eric Bana's Bruce Banner is a separate continuity — the 2008 film starts over rather than continuing this one.

title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
context: Miles Morales' animated debut and the start of Sony's animated multiverse. Separate from every live-action Spider-Man continuity.

title: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse
context: Miles takes on the Spider-Society across dozens of universes. Ends on a cliffhanger, with the concluding film not yet dated.

title: Spider-Noir (Season 1)
context: Nicolas Cage as Ben Reilly, a private investigator in 1930s New York. Live-action, from Amazon MGM and Sony, streaming in both black-and-white and colour. Its own continuity.

title: X-Men '97 (Season 1)
context: A direct continuation of X-Men: The Animated Series (1992), picking up its continuity rather than the live-action films. Made by Marvel Studios Animation, but set in its own universe — nothing here affects the MCU timeline.

title: X-Men '97 (Season 2)
context: The second season, released July 2026. A third and fourth season are in development. Still its own continuity, separate from the live-action X-Men and from the MCU.

title: Fantastic Four (2015)
context: Fox's darker reboot of the team, unconnected to the 2005 films or to Marvel Studios' The Fantastic Four: First Steps.

title: Iron Man
context: Tony Stark reveals he's Iron Man — the moment the MCU began. His Avengers Initiative conversation with Fury seeds everything that follows.

title: The Incredible Hulk
context: Bruce Banner's MCU origin. Establishes the Abomination and the tension between Bruce and the Hulk that runs all the way through Endgame. Hulk confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Iron Man 2
instruction: STOP before credits — the credits scene belongs RIGHT BEFORE Thor
context: Introduces War Machine (James Rhodes), Black Widow, and the wider S.H.I.E.L.D. world. Rhodes is confirmed for Doomsday.

title: The Consultant
instruction: Short film · Explains the bar scene from The Incredible Hulk
context: Coulson and Sitwell explain the bar scene that closes The Incredible Hulk: the World Security Council wanted Abomination for the Avengers Initiative, so S.H.I.E.L.D. sent Tony Stark to irritate General Ross into refusing. Watch it any time after The Incredible Hulk and that scene lands properly.

title: A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Thor's Hammer
context: Coulson short. Skippable.

title: Iron Man 2 (Post-Credit Scene)
context: Mjolnir is found in a New Mexico crater — the first hint that Thor's world is about to arrive on Earth.

title: Thor
instruction: STOP before credits — the credits scene belongs RIGHT BEFORE The Avengers
context: Thor's origin and Loki's discovery that he's adopted. Their rivalry defines a decade of MCU storytelling — Loki's journey from villain here ends at his sacrifice in Loki S2. Thor confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Captain America: The First Avenger (Credits)
context: Nick Fury wakes Steve in the present — he's been frozen for 70 years. Steve's disorientation here is what Endgame resolves. Steve Rogers confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Thor (Post-Credit Scene)
context: Nick Fury shows Selvig the Tesseract while Loki secretly controls his mind. The Infinity Stone chase that drives Phases 1–3 begins here.

title: The Avengers
context: The original team assembles to stop Loki and the Tesseract. The template all future team-up films follow. Mid-credits: Thanos is revealed for the first time.

title: Item 47
context: Short film set after the Battle of New York. Skippable.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 1)
context: Coulson lives post-Avengers — kept alive via alien DNA. Runs parallel to Phase 2 films. Rich S.H.I.E.L.D. lore, but no thread leads to Doomsday.

title: Iron Man 3
context: Tony's PTSD after the Battle of New York. He destroys all his suits to prove he doesn't need the armor — only to rebuild bigger in Age of Ultron.

title: Thor: The Dark World
context: The Reality Stone (Aether) is introduced and recovered. Loki fakes his death and secretly takes Odin's throne — directly setting up Ragnarok.

title: All Hail the King
context: Short film revealing the real Mandarin exists. Seeds Shang-Chi years later.

title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
context: S.H.I.E.L.D. has been HYDRA since its founding. Bucky Barnes is alive as the Winter Soldier. Steve's world is shattered — this is where the Avengers fracture begins. Bucky and Sam both confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy
context: The Power Stone and the wider cosmic MCU. Peter, Gamora, Rocket, Groot, Drax — the team whose sacrifices in Infinity War are among the most devastating.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
context: Ego (a Celestial) is Peter's father and the villain. Yondu sacrifices himself to save Peter. Emotionally the strongest Guardians film — but the team has disbanded with no confirmed Doomsday payoff.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 2)
context: Inhumans introduced. Skye revealed as Daisy Johnson/Quake. No Doomsday thread.

title: Daredevil (Season 1)
context: Matt Murdock becomes Daredevil. Wilson Fisk's origin as Kingpin. The character and world that Born Again (Doomsday-essential) continues directly.

title: Jessica Jones (Season 1)
context: Jessica vs. mind-controlling Kilgrave. Introduces Luke Cage. Outstanding character study but self-contained — no Doomsday thread.

title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
context: Tony creates Ultron from the Mind Stone — an act of hubris that creates Vision and triggers the Sokovia Accords. The Avengers fracture begins here.

title: WHiH Newsfront (Season 1)
context: In-universe news web series. Skippable.

title: Ant-Man
context: Scott Lang becomes Ant-Man. Introduces the Quantum Realm, which becomes the key to time travel in Endgame. Scott confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 3)
context: HYDRA resurrected via Inhuman parasite Hive. No Doomsday thread.

title: Daredevil (Season 2)
context: Punisher's origin and Elektra's death. The Hand is established. Feeds directly into Daredevil S3 and Defenders.

title: WHiH Newsfront (Season 2)
context: In-universe news web series. Skippable.

title: Captain America: Civil War
context: The Avengers split over the Sokovia Accords. Tony learns Bucky killed his parents. Steve and Tony's friendship fractures permanently. Spider-Man and Black Panther debut. Bucky, Sam, and Steve all confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Team Thor
context: Mockumentary revealing Thor sat out Civil War, living in Australia with his roommate Darryl. Pure comedy — no story impact.

title: Team Thor: Part 2
context: More of Thor and Darryl's roommate life before Ragnarok. Comedic — no story impact.

title: Luke Cage (Season 1)
context: Harlem's hero vs. Cottonmouth and Diamondback. Strong character work — no Doomsday thread.

title: Iron Fist (Season 1)
context: Danny Rand and the Hand. Weakest Netflix show. Context for the Defenders.

title: The Defenders (Season 1)
context: Matt, Jessica, Luke and Danny team up against the Hand. Sets up Matt's presumed death that opens Daredevil S3.

title: Black Widow
instruction: STOP before end-credits — post-credit scene belongs right before Hawkeye
context: Natasha dismantles the Red Room and frees all the Widows. Yelena Belova is introduced — she's the POV character of Thunderbolts*, which directly feeds Doomsday.

title: Eyes of Wakanda (Season 1)
instruction: 4 animated eps ~30min · Watch right before Black Panther — its ending shows how T'Challa gets his weapons.
context: Animated anthology showing Wakandan warriors through history protecting vibranium. Context for Wakanda lore.

title: Black Panther
context: T'Challa becomes king and opens Wakanda to the world. Shuri and Namor both confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
context: Peter's first MCU solo film. Tony mentors him, then steps back. The foundation for who Peter is when No Way Home breaks him.

title: The Punisher (Season 1)
context: Frank Castle's origin — a military conspiracy killed his family, and his war on the people responsible makes him the Punisher. Frank is active in the current MCU: he returns in Daredevil: Born Again, headlines The Punisher: One Last Kill, and appears in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. He is not part of Avengers: Doomsday.

title: Doctor Strange
context: Stephen Strange becomes Sorcerer Supreme. Introduces the Time Stone and the magic system. Strange's spellwork underpins No Way Home, Multiverse of Madness, and feeds Doomsday.

title: Cloak & Dagger (Season 1)
context: Tandy and Tyrone discover linked light/dark powers. Standalone Hulu series — no Doomsday thread.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 4)
context: Ghost Rider and the Darkhold — the same book Wanda uses in MoM. Rich lore, but no Doomsday thread.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.: Slingshot
context: Mini web series. Skippable.

title: Inhumans (Season 1)
context: Largely disowned by Marvel. No Doomsday connection.

title: Jessica Jones (Season 2)
context: Jessica's IGH origin. Lacks a compelling antagonist. Self-contained.

title: The New Mutants
instruction: Optional — the final Fox X-Men film.
context: A horror-tinged X-Men spinoff — five young mutants held in a secret facility. The last film of the Fox X-Men era. No MCU connection.

title: Legion (Season 1)
context: David Haller — a powerful mutant and, in the comics, Charles Xavier's son — battles his own mind and a parasitic entity. A surreal, standalone Fox X-Men show.

title: Legion (Season 2)
context: David hunts the Shadow King while his own sense of reality — and morality — unravels. Continues the surreal Fox X-Men story.

title: Legion (Season 3)
context: The final season — David uses a time-traveler to try to rewrite his past. The surreal Fox X-Men show reaches its conclusion.

title: The Gifted (Season 1)
context: A suburban family goes on the run after their children manifest mutant powers, joining an underground mutant network. Set in the Fox X-Men universe; no MCU connection.

title: The Gifted (Season 2)
context: The mutant conflict escalates as the militant Inner Circle pushes for a mutant homeland. The final season of the Fox X-Men show.

title: Luke Cage (Season 2)
context: Bushmaster vs. Mariah Dillard. Great villain — but the series was cancelled before its story could resolve.

title: Iron Fist (Season 2)
context: Danny loses the Iron Fist to Colleen Wing. Series ended here.

title: Daredevil (Season 3)
context: Fisk manipulates the FBI from inside prison. Matt reveals his identity to Karen and Foggy. Directly sets up Born Again S1 — Fisk's arc and Daredevil's public exposure both continue there.

title: Cloak & Dagger (Season 2)
context: Conclusion of the Cloak & Dagger story. No Doomsday thread.

title: Deadpool
context: Wade Wilson's origin as Deadpool. Deadpool & Wolverine (Doomsday-essential) is the direct payoff — you'll appreciate it far more having seen this.

title: Deadpool 2
context: Vanessa is killed at the start. Cable arrives from the future. Deadpool forms X-Force (most die immediately). Sets up the found-family theme that carries into Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 5)
context: Team sent to a destroyed future Earth. Coulson dies in Tahiti. No Doomsday thread.

title: Runaways (Season 1)
context: LA teens discover their parents are a supervillain cult. Standalone Hulu series — no Doomsday thread.

title: Runaways (Season 2)
context: The Runaways on the run. Jonah's alien nature revealed. No Doomsday thread.

title: Runaways (Season 3)
context: Morgan le Fay is the villain. Series finale. No Doomsday thread.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
context: Hela destroys Mjolnir and Asgard itself. Thor loses his eye. 'Asgard is not a place — it's a people.' The Asgardian refugees on their escape ship are who Thanos ambushes in the opening of Infinity War. Thor confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Team Darryl
context: The Grandmaster (from Ragnarok) becomes Darryl's new roommate on Earth. Comedic — no story impact.

title: The Punisher (Season 2)
context: Frank's Netflix run ends here, closing out the Billy Russo story. The Punisher: One Last Kill picks up after this season and leads into Frank's appearance in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. No thread from here reaches Avengers: Doomsday.

title: Jessica Jones (Season 3)
context: Series finale for Jessica and effectively the Netflix era. Standalone.

title: Venom
context: Eddie Brock bonds with the Venom symbiote. Foundation for Let There Be Carnage. Sony SSU — not MCU canon.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
instruction: STOP before credits — the credits scene belongs RIGHT AFTER Infinity War
context: Janet van Dyne is rescued from the Quantum Realm. Ghost (confirmed for Doomsday) is introduced and partially healed. The post-credits shows the snap happening in real time.

title: Avengers: Infinity War
instruction: Watch main credits. PAUSE before post-credits.
context: Thanos collects all six Infinity Stones and snaps away half of all life. Doctor Strange gives the Time Stone intentionally — 'We're in the endgame now.' This is the pivot everything before leads to and everything after responds to.

title: Ant-Man & The Wasp (All Credits)
instruction: Watch NOW immediately after Infinity War — it IS the snap happening in real time
context: Hope, Hank and Janet are snapped mid-sentence. Scott is alone in the Quantum Realm — the exact moment that makes him the key to Endgame's time heist.

title: Captain Marvel (Post-Credits Scene)
instruction: Watch NOW — directly connects to Endgame opening
context: Carol responds to Fury's pager in the Avengers facility. The direct bridge into Endgame's opening.

title: Helstrom (Season 1)
context: Demonic possession thriller. No MCU connection. Standalone.

title: Logan
instruction: Its ending is the emotional backdrop to Deadpool & Wolverine.
context: Set in 2029 — almost all mutants are gone. Logan dies protecting the next generation. His failure and sacrifice are the emotional core of Deadpool & Wolverine.

title: Avengers: Endgame
context: Five years after the snap, the surviving Avengers execute a time heist to undo it. Tony snaps Thanos away and dies. Steve stays in the past with Peggy — passing the shield to Sam. The MCU's defining film.

title: Avengers: Endgame Encore
instruction: Block out just over 3 hours. Same story as Avengers: Endgame — the ~4 minutes of new bridge footage into Doomsday only play on IMAX and Infinity Vision screens.
context: A theatrical re-release of Avengers: Endgame, timed just ahead of Doomsday. It adds a new introduction, roughly four minutes of previously unseen footage, and an end tag the Russo brothers have called a bridge into Avengers: Doomsday — though Marvel has not confirmed what it actually shows. The extra footage is exclusive to IMAX and Disney's new Infinity Vision format; standard screens show the original 2019 cut. The story itself is unchanged: if you've already seen Endgame, you already know it.

title: WandaVision (Season 1)
instruction: 9 eps · STOP before Ep 9 mid-credit scene — it's a separate entry below
context: Wanda's grief unconsciously traps an entire town in a sitcom reality. She becomes the Scarlet Witch and takes the Darkhold. White Vision is restored. The foundation of everything Multiverse of Madness builds on.

title: WandaVision (Ep 9 Mid-Credit Scene)
instruction: Watch NOW immediately after WandaVision Episode 9
context: The Scarlet Witch, studying the Darkhold in astral form, hears her children's voices — she'll chase that hope to devastating ends in Multiverse of Madness.

title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (Season 1)
context: Sam Wilson becomes Captain America. The shield passes from Steve to Sam — the arc Brave New World continues. Sam confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Loki (Season 1)
context: The TVA exists to maintain a single Sacred Timeline. He Who Remains (a Kang variant) is behind it all. Sylvie kills him — releasing every Kang variant into the multiverse. This act makes Doomsday possible.

title: What If...? (Season 1)
context: Anthology of alternate universes. Ultron gets all six Stones in one universe and goes multiverse-conquering — a preview of the multiversal chaos Doomsday brings.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 6)
context: Chronicoms invade using a Coulson lookalike. No Doomsday thread.

title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. (Season 7)
context: Chronicoms defeated via time travel through S.H.I.E.L.D. history. Series finale. No Doomsday thread.

title: Peter's To-Do List
instruction: Watch right before Far From Home.
context: Peter Parker's mundane post-Endgame to-do list. Four minutes, and it sits directly between Endgame and Far From Home.

title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
context: Peter's first adventure after Tony's death. Mysterio frames him — then reveals his identity to the world. The crisis that drives him to Doctor Strange in No Way Home.

title: Black Widow (Post-Credit Scene)
instruction: Watch NOW — directly sets up Hawkeye
context: Valentina sends Yelena to kill Clint Barton (Hawkeye) — blaming him for Natasha's death. The chain that leads to Hawkeye, then to Thunderbolts*, then to Doomsday.

title: Hawkeye (Season 1)
context: Kate Bishop becomes Hawkeye. Kingpin (Wilson Fisk) returns as the crime boss behind it all — directly setting up his Born Again arc as Mayor of New York.

title: Eternals
context: The Eternals guided humanity for thousands of years without interfering, until the Emergence forced them to choose. They stop it by killing the Celestial Tiamut, whose body is left half risen from the Indian Ocean. That body is the Celestial Island the adamantium plot of Captain America: Brave New World turns on, so this film is where it comes from. Not part of the Doomsday story.

title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
context: Shang-Chi earns the Ten Rings and defeats the Dweller-in-Darkness. A mysterious unexplained beacon is sent out — Shang-Chi confirmed for Doomsday, and the beacon is still unanswered.

title: Venom: Let There Be Carnage
context: Cletus Kasady becomes Carnage. Mid-credits: Venom briefly crosses into the MCU via Strange's NWH spell — leaving a symbiote fragment behind in the MCU timeline. That fragment is the bridge to the MCU's Venom future.

title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
instruction: Watch the Tobey & Andrew Spider-Man films first for the full payoff.
context: Peter asks Strange to make the world forget he's Spider-Man — the spell goes wrong and pulls in multiverse villains and both Tobey and Andrew's Spider-Men. Aunt May dies. All three Peters cure the villains. Strange wipes everyone's memory of Peter — he starts completely alone.

title: Morbius
context: Sony SSU. Tangential MCU link: Vulture is transported to the SSU by NWH's spell and proposes a villain team to Morbius. Widely considered poor quality.

title: The Daily Bugle (Season 1)
context: J. Jonah Jameson's in-universe anti-Spider-Man social media series. Skippable.

title: The Daily Bugle (Season 2)
context: J. Jonah Jameson's in-universe anti-Spider-Man social media series. Skippable.

title: Doctor Strange: Multiverse of Madness
context: Wanda (Scarlet Witch) is the villain — she dreamwalks universes to find her children, destroying the Illuminati including Professor X. Incursions (universe-collisions) are introduced as the multiverse's great danger. Strange confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Moon Knight (Season 1)
context: Marc Spector and Egyptian god Khonshu. Confirmed not in Doomsday — Moon Knight's next appearance is in Born Again S2 in New York.

title: Ms. Marvel (Season 1)
context: Kamala Khan — the first character explicitly called a mutant in the MCU. Her bangle connects to the Noor Dimension.

title: Thor: Love and Thunder
context: Jane Foster wields Mjolnir as the Mighty Thor — and dies of cancer after the final battle. Thor adopts Gorr's daughter Love. Love appears in Doomsday trailers. Thor confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
context: T'Challa has died. Shuri becomes the new Black Panther. Namor and Talokan are introduced. Shuri and Namor both confirmed for Doomsday.

title: She-Hulk (Season 1)
context: Jennifer Walters becomes She-Hulk. Daredevil cameo in episode 8. Fourth-wall-breaking finale. No confirmed Doomsday thread.

title: Echo (Season 1)
context: Maya Lopez standalone. Kingpin reveals his political ambitions — Mayor of New York — which Born Again S1 and S2 directly continue.

title: Ironheart (Season 1)
context: Riri Williams builds her Iron Heart suit in Chicago, and takes on The Hood.

title: Werewolf by Night
context: Halloween special. Jack Russell is the Werewolf by Night. Elsa Bloodstone claims the Bloodstone. Standalone — no Doomsday thread.

title: GOTG Holiday Special
context: Mantis is revealed as Peter's half-sister. The Guardians give Peter Knowhere as a Christmas gift. Fun — but zero Doomsday relevance.

title: I Am Groot (Season 1)
context: Baby Groot animated shorts. No Doomsday thread.

title: I Am Groot (Season 2)
context: Teen Groot animated shorts. No Doomsday thread.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
context: Scott and Cassie fight Kang the Conqueror in the Quantum Realm. Kang is defeated — and the post-credits shows the Council of Kangs alarmed that he was killed by ants. The Kang threat is fully unleashed.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
context: Rocket's heartbreaking origin — experimented on by the High Evolutionary. The team's emotional farewell: Peter returns to Earth, Rocket leads new Guardians. No confirmed Doomsday payoff.

title: Venom: The Last Dance
context: Tom Hardy's final Venom film. Knull the symbiote god is the true threat. Eddie dies. Sony SSU finale — no direct MCU connection.

title: Madame Web
context: A New York paramedic with clairvoyant powers protects three young women from a spider-powered villain hunting them. Sony’s Spider-Man Universe; disconnected from the MCU.

title: Kraven the Hunter
context: Sergei Kravinoff gains animal-like abilities and becomes the ruthless hunter Kraven, turning on his crime-lord father. Sony’s Spider-Man Universe; disconnected from the MCU.

title: Secret Invasion (Season 1)
context: Rogue Skrulls attempt a nuclear attack. Fury's post-Endgame Skrull replacement revealed. No confirmed Doomsday payoff.

title: The Marvels
context: Carol, Kamala and Monica's powers become entangled — they swap places when using them. Monica enters a hole in space and ends up in an alternate universe.

title: Marvel Zombies
context: Alternate universe zombie apocalypse. Not Sacred Timeline. No Doomsday connection.

title: Loki (Season 2)
context: Loki sacrifices himself — becoming the new Yggdrasil (World Tree), holding all branching timelines together with his own power. His sacrifice is the reason the multiverse is stable enough for Doomsday to happen at all.

title: What If...? (Season 2)
context: Anthology S2. Happy Hogan gets Iron Man powers briefly. Kahhori — a Mohawk hero empowered by the Tesseract — is introduced. Entertaining alt-stories with no direct Doomsday thread.

title: What If...? (Season 3)
context: Peggy Carter's story is finally concluded. Tony appears across realities. The Watcher's role in the multiverse war grows. The last anthology chapter — directly precedes Doomsday.

title: Deadpool & Wolverine
instruction: Watch Logan before this for full impact.
context: The TVA is erasing the Fox universe. Wade and Logan must save it. They defeat Cassandra Nova and save the Fox timeline — which is why the entire original X-Men cast can appear in Doomsday. This film is the bridge.

title: Agatha All Along (Season 1)
context: Agatha leads a coven through the Witches Road. Billy Maximoff (Wanda's son) is revealed as Teen Wiccan. Self-contained witch mythology — no confirmed Doomsday connection.

title: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man (Season 1)
context: Animated — not MCU canon. Alternate Peter Parker story where Norman Osborn is an early mentor. Unconnected to Tom Holland's continuity.

title: Daredevil: Born Again (Season 1)
context: Fisk is Mayor of New York. Matt is openly Daredevil. This is the culmination of the entire Netflix Daredevil run.

title: Captain America: Brave New World
context: Sam Wilson as Captain America defeats Red Hulk (Thaddeus Ross). The Leader is the hidden manipulator. Sam's arc from FATWS completes here — he's confirmed as a major Doomsday character.

title: Thunderbolts*
context: Yelena Belova leads a team of anti-heroes against the Void (Bob Reynolds / Sentry's shadow). They emerge as the New Avengers. This is the team going into Doomsday.

title: Wonder Man (Season 1)
instruction: 8 eps · All dropped Jan 27 2026 · Marvel Spotlight.
context: Simon Williams — Hollywood actor with ionic powers. Standalone Marvel Spotlight series. Rumoured but not officially confirmed for Doomsday.

title: Daredevil: Born Again (Season 2)
instruction: 8 eps · Premieres Mar 24 2026 · Concurrent with The Punisher: One Last Kill.
context: Fisk hunts all vigilantes as Mayor — Daredevil is public enemy number one. Matt builds an army from the shadows. Moon Knight appears in New York.

title: The Punisher: One Last Kill
context: Frank Castle tries to leave violence behind but is pulled into an unexpected conflict. Jon Bernthal. Concurrent with Born Again S2.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
context: Peter fights crime full-time as Spider-Man in a world that no longer remembers him, and the strain of watching his friends move on sparks a transformation he can barely control. A shocking new threat forces him to fight for the city and everyone he loves. The last MCU film before Doomsday. Jon Bernthal appears as Frank Castle / the Punisher.

title: VisionQuest (Season 1)
instruction: 8 eps · Mid-to-late 2026 · Watch WandaVision and Agatha All Along first.
context: White Vision — restored with all his memories at the end of WandaVision — searches for his identity. James Spader returns as Ultron. Completes the WandaVision trilogy. Airs in the window before Doomsday.

title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
context: Doctor Doom makes his MCU debut — set in an alternate 1960s. Galactus and the Silver Surfer appear. Post-credits: Doom crosses into the main MCU timeline. The direct setup for Doomsday.

title: AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY
context: Everything leads here.
